check_text:
protocol.py: 3 biology problems (1 error, 2 notes).

1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from tube A2 in slot 2: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 67:  p20.aspirate(1, tubes["A2"])
   At line 67 the p20_single_gen2 draws 1 ul from polymerase (tube A2 in slot 2) with its
   tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 4 ul, which in this
   Opentrons 24 Tube Rack with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap reaches only 0.89 mm up: the tip is above
   the liquid and draws air (this line did it once, after 11 times in the liquid; 1 ul of
   air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 1 well
   filled from these draws got air instead of liquid.
   Affected: tube A2 in slot 2.
   Also reached 1 other well: well A12 in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 6 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [b08b478441fd]

2. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 11 wells of polymerase with a sample
   line 68:  p20.dispense(0.5, plate[f"A{i}"])
   At line 68 the robot starts putting polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full
   Skirt (slot 3), and 11 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate
   holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8
   and 3 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 0.5 ul of polymerase and 2 ul of water in place
   of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [deaf5fecf614]

3. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 11 wells never mixed after polymerase went in (2% of the well)
   line 68:  p20.dispense(0.5, plate[f"A{i}"])
   At line 68 the robot added polymerase to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more
   in slot 3, which already held buffer, sample 1, fwd primer, rev primer and 11 more (this
   line did it 11 times). The addition was 2% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be,
   mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3 after line 68:
   `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [99777fd60071]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: The pipette draws air from tube A2 in slot 2: the liquid is below the tip
findings.explanation: At line 67 the p20_single_gen2 draws 1 ul from polymerase (tube A2 in slot 2) with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 4 ul, which in this Opentrons 24 Tube Rack with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap reaches only 0.89 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it once, after 11 times in the liquid; 1 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 1 well filled from these draws got air instead of liquid.
findings.fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 6 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.

findings.title: No no-template control: 11 wells of polymerase with a sample
findings.explanation: At line 68 the robot starts putting polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt (slot 3), and 11 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3.
findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 0.5 ul of polymerase and 2 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: 11 wells never mixed after polymerase went in (2% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 68 the robot added polymerase to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3, which already held buffer, sample 1, fwd primer, rev primer and 11 more (this line did it 11 times). The addition was 2% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3 after line 68: `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
